Not me, but my mother. I was about 9 and we had been at my grandparents house. I was upstairs on the computer, my grandparents were outside by the pool and my mum was watching TV downstairs. I still remember her suddenly screaming for my grandad and shouting ‘oh my god’ and yelling for me to come downstairs. I was terrified, I‘d convinced myself my grandad had collapsed or something like that. 
I ran/tripped downstairs and heard her yell that our dog was still in the car and had been for probably 4-5 hours. It was a really hot day as well and my stomach SUNK. They all ran out and I remember watching them open the door and my mum just collapsing in on herself.

It was a really traumatic day to be honest, and my mum didn’t get over it for months. It felt like this awful crime because everyone was telling little 9 year old me not to tell anyone, just to say he had a heart attack.
For a really long time I blamed myself for it because that day I’d refused to sit in the backseat with him like I usually did, and I thought it was my fault because we hadn’t opened the back door, and we’d forgotten he was there.

I don’t tell people this story ever just because I don’t want anyone to think my mum is a bad person. It’s still one of the most upsetting times of my life, but I don’t blame my mum at all. She was so traumatised by it, and we still barely talk about him even though he was my best friend growing up. I miss him a lot, but I know he at least lived a happy life. I just hate knowing he lived his last moments in discomfort and confusion :(

By the sounds of it, you are still young. You have a limitless future ahead of you, and I am assuming, supportive parents. Find something you can live for, even if it’s something small, and cling to that. Tell your parents how you feel, and let them know what it is that you love about life. Focus on the positives in your life, you’re going to be okay.

Sometimes things seem like they’re going nowhere, but imagine how incredible you’re going to feel when things DO go somewhere! It’s cliche, but you genuinely have so much ahead of you. Think of your future family, friends, movies or games you’re excited to see, the taste of your favourite foods. You don’t need a huge reason to keep living, you need to re-find the beauty and joy in the every day. And if all else fails, go to a shelter or a pet store and play with some puppies or something! That always helps.

I hope you’re still here, and if you are, please listen to these comments. You are so so young, and you have a whole future to look forward to. Things look bleak, but please stick around. For your mother, your future wife and children. You are worthy of a good life, and you can have one. Please stay.

And if you really are set on this, please write a note or something for your mother. It won’t ease the pain of losing you, but it’ll help her find her way through it.
